doing the following: e^coefficient. That is raise e (2.71828) to the
power of the regression coefficient. Example: coefficient = 0.245,
then e^0.245=1.278. So OR = 1.278.

Davester

messages.subject: probably a bug in Deducer - Data viewer - Open Data Frame
messages.subject_clean: probably a bug in Deducer - Data viewer - Open Data Frame
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I think that I found a bug in the Deducer modul, which is responsible
for opening csv files.

I am usually confronted with files from students for statistical
evaluation. Some of them contain hypens in the name, for example xx-yy-
zz.csv

When such files are opened with the Data viewer - Open Data Frame
module it tried to generate the name for the data.frame based on the
filename.

The execution ends with an error, because the hypens are interpreted
as a minus sign.

The error message is: object xx not found.

You might say, just avoid such filenames. That's a good suggestion.
But I think that is should be possible to catch such an error and
replace the "minus" (hyphen) in the filename and replace it with an
underscore or just omit it.

I hope the description is precise enough.

 maybe this is helpful, too:

R version 2.13.0 (2011-04-13)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Package Deducer version 0.4-4
Package rJava version 0.8-8

java version "1.6.0_24"
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.6.0_24-b07)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 19.1-b02, mixed mode)

Sincerely

Karl-Heinz

messages.subject: Linear Regression Coefficients
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

New user here. . .

I've built a linear regression model where I wish to see certain
variables interacting (var1*var2), but the individual variables by
themselves var1, var2 are not in the model.  After running the model,
I see coefficients for each of the variables individually in addition
to coefficients for the interacting variables. What is the meaning of
the coefficients of individual variables if they are not in the model
except where they are part of an interacting variable?

In the results, would I use the coeffiecients for variables in the
model only and ignore the rest?
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: Linear Regression Coefficients

the * operator includes all lower level interactions. you are looking for :

Example:
lm(formula=mpg ~ cyl:hp,data=mtcars,na.action=na.omit)

messages.subject: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni
messages.subject_clean: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I found a reproducible syntax error when I run a K-Sample Test with
pairwise comparison (method t-Test, correction Bonferroni).

This is the output in the console

> k.sample.test(formula=d(depVar) ~ indepFactor,
+ data=demo,
+ test=oneway.test,var.equal=TRUE)
                           One-way analysis of
means
              F (num df,denom df)      p-value
depVar 14.70871            (2,27) 4.778948e-05
> pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo$indepFactorpool.sd = TRUE, p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')
Fehler: Unerwartete(s) '=' in "pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo
$indepFactorpool.sd ="
>
The cause of the error is a missing comma before pool.sd <http://pool.sd>. If you
correct it to:

pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo$indepFactor, pool.sd <http://pool.sd> = TRUE,
p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')

The statistics is calculated.

Cheers

Karl-Heinz

messages.subject: Re: Error with paired sample t-tests
messages.body_plain:
I wondered if this was the problem - specifying a one-sided
alternative hypothesis for a 95% CI. A confidence interval for a
statistic makes the most sense when a two-sided alternative hypothesis
is used, otherwise one of the limits is listed as infinity. Change the
alternative hypothesis to two-sided and things will probably be fine.

Davester

messages.subject_clean: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I was just curious whether I could fix the problem myself, however, I
have to mention that I have not much experience in programming.

It looks to me as if the problem is located in the file: /org/rosuda/
deducer/menu/KSampleDialog.java line 438 in the latest svn source.
Beginning in line 435 the source currently looks like:

435	...		}else if(pairwiseMethod == "t-test (equal variance)"){
436				for(int i=0;i<variables.size();i++)
437					cmd += "pairwise.t.test(" +subn + "$" +
variables.get(i).toString() + "," +
438										subn + "$" + factor + "pool.sd <http://pool.sd> = TRUE" +
439										", p.adjust.method = '" + model.pairwiseCorrection +"')
\n";

My problem should be fixed with line 438 being changed to (note the
comma before pool.sd <http://pool.sd>):

438										subn + "$" + factor + ", pool.sd <http://pool.sd> = TRUE" +

I have no idea, how to upload this fix to the repository (I have never
worked with svn so far). It would be great if anybody else could
upload the fix, please.

Thanks a lot

Sincerely

Karl-Heinz

messages.subject: facet_grid rows~cols reversed and facet_wrap nrow issue
messages.subject_clean: facet_grid rows~cols reversed and facet_wrap nrow issue
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
   It looks to me that the rows and columns boxes are reversed in
facet_grid compared with the call that I expected of facets = rowvar ~
colvar.

In addition, when using facet_wrap - Wrap options, it appears as
though # of rows is currently only added to the call or updated when
changed if ncol is specified although you can specify or update ncol
without specifying nrow.

Thanks, Deducer is a great tool!
-Allan
